questions.question: Brownian motion describes which of the following phenomena?
options: The random motion of particles suspended in a medium.
The settling of heavy particles at the bottom of a container.
The chemical reaction between an acid and an alkali.
The change of state from a liquid to a gas during boiling.

questions.question: What happens to the movement of particles in a gas or a solution when the temperature is increased?
options: They slow down and become tightly packed.
They move more quickly.
They stop moving completely.
They only move in a single direction.

questions.question: Why is a suspension not considered a true solution?
options: The solid particles can be seen and will eventually settle over time.
It consists of only one pure substance.
The liquid evaporates instantly when mixed.
The particles are too small to be filtered out.

questions.question: When mixing 50 cm³ of water and 50 cm³ of ethanol, the total volume is slightly less than 100 cm³. What is the explanation for this?
options: Some of the liquid evaporated instantly.
One type of particle fits into the spaces between the other type of particle.
The particles expanded and took up less space.
Mass was destroyed during the mixing process.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares dissolving and melting?
options: Dissolving requires heat to break bonds, while melting requires a solvent.
Melting is a chemical change, whereas dissolving is a physical change.
Both are physical processes, but they are not the same thing.
Dissolving and melting are identical chemical reactions.

questions.question: Why must scientific methods be written clearly?
options: To guarantee that the experiment will always produce the exact same speed of reaction.
So that they are both repeatable and reproducible.
To make sure no other scientist can copy the experiment.
To allow the experiment to be carried out without any equipment.

questions.question: How is a solution formed in chemistry?
options: When a soluble solid dissolves in an appropriate solvent.
When an insoluble solid settles at the bottom of a beaker of water.
When a gas turns directly into a solid without becoming a liquid.
When two liquids are stirred together and form two distinct layers.

questions.question: If 10 g of salt is completely dissolved in 100 g of water, what is the total mass of the resulting salt solution?
Which piece of equipment and unit should be used to measure the volume of a liquid?
options: A balance, measuring in grams (g)
A thermometer, measuring in degrees Celsius (°C)
A ruler, measuring in centimetres (cm)
A measuring cylinder, measuring in cubic centimetres (cm³)

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of a pure material regarding its physical properties?
options: It melts and boils over a wide range of temperatures.
It has a fixed melting point and boiling point.
Its boiling point changes every time it is measured.
It does not have any melting point.

questions.question: What effect do impurities have on the melting and boiling points of a material?
options: They keep the melting and boiling points exactly the same.
They change the melting and boiling point of the material.
They prevent the material from ever changing state.
They only affect the boiling point, never the melting point.

questions.question: How do mixtures behave when they are heated to melt or boil?
options: They melt or boil at a single, precise temperature.
They melt or boil over a range of temperatures.
They do not melt or boil at all.
They only change state when a catalyst is added.

questions.question: At a given temperature, what is true about the amount of solute that can dissolve in a solvent?
options: There is a limit to how much solute can dissolve.
An infinite amount of solute can always dissolve.
No solute can dissolve unless the mixture is stirred.
The solute will always float on top of the solvent.

questions.question: What often happens to dissolved solutes as a hot solution is allowed to cool down?
options: They turn into gas and escape.
They may become insoluble and form crystals.
They multiply in mass.
They chemically react to form water.

questions.question: In a scientific graph, how can a line of best fit be helpful?
options: It shows the exact location of every anomalous result.
It helps to identify and describe relationships between variables.
It guarantees that the experiment was carried out perfectly.
It removes the need to collect any actual data.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of factors can affect the solubility of a substance?
options: The size of the solute pieces, the choice of solvent, or the temperature of the solvent.
Only the color of the container and the time of day.
The room's air pressure and the mass of the beaker.
Only the shape of the stirring rod used.

questions.question: In an investigation, what is the independent variable?
options: The variable that is kept the same to keep the test fair.
The variable that is observed or measured.
The variable that is changed by the investigator.
The variable that has no effect on the results.

questions.question: What is the definition of the dependent variable in a science experiment?
options: The factor that the scientist decides to change.
The factor that is observed or measured during the investigation.
The equipment used to record the time.
The substance that remains unchanged throughout.

questions.question: What name is given to the variables that are kept the same throughout an investigation?
options: Independent variables
Dependent variables
Control variables
Uncontrolled variables

questions.question: Why do we only change the variable being tested in a fair test?
options: To make the experiment run as quickly as possible.
So that it is clear that it made a difference to the results.
To ensure that the equipment does not break.
To make the graph easier to draw by hand.
